description:
In this video, we explore linear types and how they are implemented in Haskell. We study some theoretical background on linear types, look at the LinearTypes extension, and list some of the perks that linear types can bring to the table. 

Additional resources: 

The "LinearTypes" GHC extension: https://downloads.haskell.org/ghc/latest/docs/users_guide/exts/linear_types.html
Linear types, as described in the GHC documentation: https://gitlab.haskell.org/ghc/ghc/-/wikis/linear-types
Linear Haskell: practical linearity in a higher-order polymorphic language / Bernardy J. et al.: https://arxiv.org/abs/1710.09756
Linear types make performance more predictable: https://www.tweag.io/blog/2017-03-13-linear-types/
Linearly Qualified Types: Generic inference for capabilities and uniqueness / Spiwack A. et al.: https://arxiv.org/abs/2103.06127
Linear Logic: https://plato.stanford.edu/entries/logic-linear/
